steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write a section for an encyclopedia article on aromaticity in cheminformatics that goes through the aromaticity models offered by the major toolkits (CDK, RDKit, OpenEye OEChem, Open Babel, Indigo).

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Intro: toolkits differ, often several options
- Chemistry Development Kit (CDK)
- RDKit
- OpenEye OEChem
- Open Babel
- Indigo

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Intro: different toolkits, different aromaticity models, often multiple options
- CDK (cite)
  - highly configurable: electron donation models + cycle finders
  - donation models: CDK model (needs atom type perception, no exocyclic π-bonds); CDK allowing exocyclic (exocyclic double bonds ok); Daylight model (Daylight/OpenSMILES spec); Pi bonds model (only atoms adjacent to cyclic π-bonds, MDL-like)
  - cycle finders: MCB/SSSR, relevant, essential, all cycles, CDK aromatic set (MCB + envelope rings for small fused systems)
- RDKit (cite)
  - AROMATICITY_RDKIT default, rule-based, 4n+2, fused systems
  - AROMATICITY_SIMPLE: 5- and 6-membered rings only
  - AROMATICITY_MDL: MDL/BIOVIA definition
  - AROMATICITY_MMFF94: MMFF force field rules
  - AROMATICITY_CUSTOM: user-defined functions
  - perception limited to fused-ring systems, members at most 24 atoms, for efficiency
- OpenEye OEChem TK (cite)
  - five models: OpenEye (default), Daylight, Tripos, MDL, MMFF
  - differ on heteroatoms, exocyclic bonds, unusual rings
  - Kekulization verification not strict Hückel; keeps user-specified aromaticity from input
- Open Babel (cite)
  - single model close to Daylight
  - OBAromaticTyper class, pattern-based rules
  - re-perceives when writing SMILES, consistent output
- Indigo (cite)
  - basic model: no external double bonds for aromatic rings
  - generic model: external double bonds allowed

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Different cheminformatics toolkits implement different aromaticity models, and they often provide more than one option:

### Chemistry Development Kit (CDK)

The Chemistry Development Kit has a highly configurable aromaticity system, which combines electron donation models with cycle finders:

Electron donation models:

CDK model: atom type perception is required; exocyclic π-bonds are not allowed

CDK allowing exocyclic: the same as the CDK model but exocyclic double bonds are permitted

Daylight model: follows the Daylight/OpenSMILES specification

Pi bonds model: only atoms next to cyclic π-bonds contribute (like MDL)

Cycle finders:

MCB/SSSR

Relevant cycles

Essential cycles

All cycles

CDK aromatic set (MCB plus envelope rings for small fused systems)

### RDKit

RDKit has several aromaticity models:

AROMATICITY_RDKIT (the default): rule-based, follows 4n+2 and takes fused systems into account

AROMATICITY_SIMPLE: perception is restricted to 5- and 6-membered rings

AROMATICITY_MDL: follows the MDL/BIOVIA definition of aromaticity

AROMATICITY_MMFF94: uses the aromaticity rules of the MMFF force field

AROMATICITY_CUSTOM: lets the user define aromaticity functions

For computational efficiency, aromaticity perception is limited to fused-ring systems where all the members are at most 24 atoms in size.

### OpenEye OEChem

- five models: OpenEye (default), Daylight, Tripos, MDL, MMFF
- differ on heteroatoms, exocyclic bonds, unusual rings
- Kekulization verification instead of strict Hückel -> user-specified aromaticity kept

### Open Babel

- one model, close to Daylight
- OBAromaticTyper class, pattern-based rules
- re-perceives on SMILES output for consistency

### Indigo

- basic model: no external double bonds for aromatic rings
- generic model: external double bonds allowed

Different cheminformatics toolkits implement different aromaticity models, and they often provide more than one option:

### Chemistry Development Kit (CDK)

The Chemistry Development Kit has a highly configurable aromaticity system, which combines electron donation models with cycle finders:

Electron donation models:

CDK model: atom type perception is required; exocyclic π-bonds are not allowed

CDK allowing exocyclic: the same as the CDK model but exocyclic double bonds are permitted

Daylight model: follows the Daylight/OpenSMILES specification

Pi bonds model: only atoms next to cyclic π-bonds contribute (like MDL)

Cycle finders:

MCB/SSSR

Relevant cycles

Essential cycles

All cycles

CDK aromatic set (MCB plus envelope rings for small fused systems)

### RDKit

RDKit has several aromaticity models:

AROMATICITY_RDKIT (the default): rule-based, follows 4n+2 and takes fused systems into account

AROMATICITY_SIMPLE: perception is restricted to 5- and 6-membered rings

AROMATICITY_MDL: follows the MDL/BIOVIA definition of aromaticity

AROMATICITY_MMFF94: uses the aromaticity rules of the MMFF force field

AROMATICITY_CUSTOM: lets the user define aromaticity functions

For computational efficiency, aromaticity perception is limited to fused-ring systems where all the members are at most 24 atoms in size.

### OpenEye OEChem

There are five aromaticity models supported by OpenEye OEChem TK:

OpenEye (the default)

Daylight

Tripos

MDL

MMFF

These models are quite different in how they treat heteroatoms, exocyclic bonds and unusual ring systems. OpenEye does not use strict Hückel evaluation, it uses Kekulization verification instead, and this means user-specified aromaticity from input files can be preserved.

### Open Babel

Open Babel has a single aromaticity model, which is close to the Daylight definition. Aromaticity perception is done by the OBAromaticTyper class, using pattern-based rules. When it writes SMILES, the toolkit re-perceives aromaticity, so that the output is consistent no matter what aromaticity annotations the input had.

### Indigo

Indigo has two aromaticity models:

Basic model: external double bonds are not allowed for aromatic rings

Generic model: external double bonds are allowed
